segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast we have real conversations in

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: easy English to help you learn. I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: And I'm Phil. And you can find a video version of this podcast with

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: subtitles to help you on our website. And that's bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hi Phil, how are you doing?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: I'm doing very well. What about you, Beth? How's your day?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm okay. I am a little bit tired. As you know, I'm pregnant and my baby is kicking me

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: right now as we record this. And it's funny because today we're talking about having children

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and being parents.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Oh, yes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So you have children, don't you?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Yes, I have two. I've got a 12-year-old and a 14-year-old.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So you almost have two teenagers, which sounds a bit stressful.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: It can be sometimes but yeah it can be sometimes because it might be that they have a problem and you can see they got a problem but they don want to tell you what it is Okay So that can be stressful

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think that a problem I won have yet Although a baby crying they can really tell you what the problem is

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: No, I think it's probably much more tiring when children are younger, I think.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So what would you say are the positives of raising children?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: When you raise a child, that means you take care of them and support them while they grow.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So what are the benefits of raising children?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: So I think one of the best things about parenting is just it is so rewarding when you see them doing something new,

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: something they've learned to do. And when they get to the age of my kids, they start doing things that I can't do.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: So it's like, wow, you're doing better than me. This is good.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What can your children do that you can't do?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: play the saxophone, speak Chinese really well, speak Japanese.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Wow.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: All these things. I can't do those. Not to that level.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, amazing. Great.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So what are the difficulties of being a new parent?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: It's a long time ago for me.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: I trying to remember but when you have very young children it can be very intense There not much of a break because you have to do everything for them

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: So you don't get much of a rest.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: It gets a bit easier when they become toddlers, when they're sort of two or three and running around, although that has its own problems.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Don't they have a lot of tantrums when they are toddlers?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So lying on the floor, screaming.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Yeah, I mean, toddlers do have lots of tantrums, but you learn to deal with those.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So what advice do you have for me as a new parent?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: OK, I think I've got two big pieces of advice.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: And the first one is that when you have kids, things change very quickly as they grow and they get different and everything gets different and you can't go back.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: So enjoy what's happening when it's happening.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: And the second piece of advice is don't give them your phone.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Those are two very good pieces of advice, I think.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Thank you.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Especially living in the moment.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think that's very important.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK let recap the vocabulary we heard during the podcast

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We heard the word pregnant.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: If you are pregnant, then you have a baby growing inside you.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Like me, I am pregnant.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: If you raise a child, you take care of them and support them while they grow.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Parenting is the act of raising a child and that comes from the verb to parent.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Phil said that parenting can be very rewarding but very stressful.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: We also had toddler. Now, a toddler is a young child who's just starting to walk

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: and we also said that they often have tantrums, which is when they get angry and scream and shout a lot.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English. Why not try the worksheet on our website to test what you've learnt? That's at bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: And we'll be back next week with another conversation in Easy English. See you then!

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Goodbye!

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Bye!
